correctness.rationale: No composable pair means products of arrows vanish and loops are excluded. Vertex labels are independent uniform F_q² values; conditioning on them separates the arrows. Each coefficient is forced zero at equal endpoints and is uniform otherwise, by a nonzero linear functional of the independent arrow variables. On a forest, changing variables to component roots and oriented edge differences is bijective, so the full field-valued coefficients are mutually independent, including for the empty set. For arbitrary T, expanding the zero-probability product gives joint zero probability minus the product of its marginals as q^(−|T|) times the sum over F⊆T of (q−1)^|F| times [q^(−2r(F))−q^(−2|F|)]. This is nonnegative term by term and strictly positive if T contains a circuit, including two parallel edges; characteristic plays no role. The original contraction/chromatic fiber and zero specialization follow by the same equality constraints, and its forest product uses q² roots per component and q³+q²−q or q³−q lifts per edge. The original checker tests the all-zero witness rather than every entry of the product law and was inspected, not run. The independent replay and the separately run repaired checker test all marginal entries exactly over a quiver with a four-cycle, parallel edges and an isolated vertex: 22 of 32 subsets factor over 1,048,576 input pairs, exactly matching leaf pruning.

value.rationale: The repaired criterion determines exactly which observed subsets of a labelled random bracket have product laws, and reconstructs the graphic matroid including minimal dependence from parallel arrows and longer cycles. It distinguishes genuine mutual independence from pairwise independence (for example on a four-cycle without parallel arrows), and gives a single-event witness of failure on every nonforest. This is a useful structural reading of the commutator law, not a recomputation of the existing complete fibers.
